title: Self-Inductance and Mutual Inductance

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Electromagnetic Induction

explanation: Self-inductance L quantifies a coil's opposition to CHANGES in its own current — an induced EMF (by Lenz's law, opposing the change) is proportional to the rate of change of current in the same coil. Mutual inductance M quantifies how a changing current in one coil induces an EMF in a NEARBY, separate coil (the basis of transformers). For a long solenoid, L = μ₀n²Al depends on turns density squared, area, and length — showing why tightly-wound, long coils give large inductance.

variables.meaning: Number of turns per unit length
Cross-sectional area and length of the solenoid

workedExample.scenario: A coil with L = 2 H has current changing at dI/dt = 5 A/s.
workedExample.result: ε = −10 V (opposing the increase, per Lenz's law)

commonMistakes: Forgetting the negative sign (Lenz's law) — the induced EMF always opposes the change causing it, not supports it.
Confusing self-inductance (EMF induced in the SAME coil) with mutual inductance (EMF induced in a DIFFERENT, nearby coil).
genZNote: Lenz's law: the induced EMF is always petty and opposes whatever change caused it.
